newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Milosevic resigns as Serbian president.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic resigns as Serbian president.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on Wednesday relinquished his post so he could assume the office of Yugoslav federal president later in the day, Tanjug news agency reported.

In a letter to Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic, Milosevic said that in line with the Serbian constitution Tomic now took over the post of acting Serbian president until the presidential elections due within 60 days.
Milosevic, 55, was later sworn in as Yugoslav president.
The dominant figure in Yugoslav politics since the breakup of the six-member federation in the early 1990s, he was prevented by the Serbian constitution from serving any further term.
His switch to the Yugoslav presidency, formerly a relatively unimportant post, was generally interpreted as a tactic to remain effective political supremo in Belgrade.
